result.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models
result.summary: The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has significantly enhanced the capabilities of agents across various tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) loops, in which a language model repeatedly rewrites a program and builds on its previous version, now perform well in machine-learning tasks, but they rely on frontier models and hundreds of calls per run. Small open-weight models are far cheaper, yet when used alone, their programs often crash and their improvements stall. We propose DiVE (diverse models evolve), an ensemble method for RSI that aims to improve creativity and diversity of generated solutions. DiVE uses three components: a shared memory, a failure log, and best-idea-wins rounds. This allows models to write candidate solutions from the same context and retain the best idea at each iteration. On 22 MLE-bench Lite competitions, an ensemble of five 8-12B open-weight models has 25.4% less test error than its average member and 16.7% less than Llama 3.3 70B, and comes within 7.1% of Qwen 3.5 122B-A10B at 75% of its cost. Diversity among small models can thus stand in for part of the scale that RSI relies on.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DiVE，用共享记忆、失败日志与「最佳想法胜出」轮次组织五个 8–12B 开源小模型的集成来做程序递归自我改进，在 MLE-bench Lite 上以较低成本接近更大模型的表现，主张模型多样性可部分替代规模。
